context.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for fraud analysts. It operates within AWS eu-west-1, adhering strictly to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems (External Actor)
- Fraud Analysts (Internal User)
- Card Networks / Token Vaults (External System)
- Audit / Compliance Archive (External Storage)
- ML Model / Rule Registry (External System)
- API Gateway / Ingress Service (AWS ECS Fargate / Envoy)
- Scoring Engine (Stateless microservice in Rust/Go)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js/Python API)
- Data & Event Tiers (Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon SQS / Kinesis)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Sends authorization requests via gRPC over HTTP/2.
- Scoring Engine -> Card Networks / Token Vaults: Resolves tokens via secure API over mTLS.
- Scoring Engine -> Audit / Compliance Archive: Streams audit logs asynchronously via HTTPS / TLS 1.3.
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Backend: Accesses case management via HTTPS.
- ML Engineers -> ML Model / Rule Registry: Pushes model and rule updates via HTTPS / REST API.
- Scoring Engine -> Payment Gateway: Sends circuit breaker signals via gRPC for fail-open fallback.

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Cloud provider utilizing AWS PrivateLink for perimeter security within VPC Private Subnets.
- gRPC / Protocol Buffers: High-performance binary serialization to meet the sub-50ms P99 latency requirement.
- Rust / Go: Low-level stateless execution for the Scoring Engine to handle 3,000 TPS under tight latency bounds.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Low-latency NoSQL data store for real-time state and rules.
- Amazon SQS / Kinesis: Asynchronous event streaming for tamper-evident 7-year audit logs.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict sub-50ms P99 decision latency and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance using lightweight AWS managed services. It respects the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operational limits of a three-engineer team while satisfying 7-year auditability and high availability.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
A real-time payment fraud screening and case management system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations in AWS eu-west-1. It delivers sub-50ms fraud decisions while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts and ML Engineers (Users)
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems and Card Networks / Token Vaults (External Systems)
* AWS API Gateway (Ingestion Router)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go on AWS ECS Fargate)
* ML Inference Service (Python with ONNX Runtime on AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Backend (Go/Node.js on AWS ECS Fargate)
* Fraud Analyst Frontend (Amazon CloudFront and S3)
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis Feature Store)
* Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3 Object Lock (Data Storage & Audit Archive)
* Amazon EventBridge (Event Bus)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to AWS API Gateway: mTLS over HTTPS / gRPC
* AWS API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine: gRPC
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to ML Inference Service: Internal gRPC
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): TCP (RESP)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine and Case Management Backend to Amazon DynamoDB: HTTPS (AWS SDK)
* DynamoDB Streams to Amazon S3 Object Lock: AWS Internal Stream
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon EventBridge: HTTPS (AWS SDK)
* Amazon EventBridge to Case Management Backend: HTTPS / Webhook
* Fraud Analyst Frontend to Case Management Backend: HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen to minimize operational overhead for a 3-person team within a €25k/month budget.
* Go: Powers the Real-Time Scoring Engine and Case Management Backend to guarantee P99 latency below 50ms at 3,000 TPS.
* Python with ONNX Runtime: Powers the ML Inference Service to enable zero-downtime model updates and fast scoring execution.
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides low-latency feature lookups for context hydration.
* Amazon DynamoDB with S3 Object Lock: Delivers scalable storage and tamper-evident 7-year auditability via WORM storage.
* Amazon EventBridge: Handles asynchronous, event-driven case routing.

## Rationale
This architecture combines lightweight AWS Fargate containers with Go and ONNX runtimes to meet strict P99 latency and high-throughput demands. It achieves PCI-DSS compliance and tamper-evident 7-year audit logging using serverless AWS services within a fixed budget and small team capacity.

AWS API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations and manages suspicious payment reviews for a mid-size payment processor. It uses an AWS-based cloud architecture to provide low-latency scoring, strict security, and tamper-evident auditing.

## Key Elements
- **AWS WAF**: Edge security filter for IP reputation and geo-fencing.
- **AWS API Gateway HTTP API**: Public-facing ingress router for incoming payment requests.
- **Authentication & mTLS Validator**: Enforces transport security via Mutual TLS.
- **Payload Validator & Schema Enforcer**: Validates incoming request structures using JSON Schema.
- **Rate Limiter & Throttling Controller**: Protects downstream services from traffic spikes and DDoS attacks.
- **Internal Service Registry**: AWS Cloud Map for dynamic container endpoint resolution.
- **Audit Log Redactor / Sanitizer**: Strips cleartext card data from logs for PCI-DSS compliance.
- **Metrics & Telemetry Emitter**: Amazon CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray for tracing and monitoring.

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems -> AWS WAF**: Inspects inbound requests via `HTTPS`.
- **AWS WAF -> Authentication & mTLS Validator**: Forwards filtered traffic via `HTTPS`.
- **Authentication & mTLS Validator -> Payload Validator**: Passes authenticated traffic internally via `HTTP/2`.
- **Payload Validator -> Real-Time Scoring Engine**: Routes validated payloads using `gRPC via AWS VPC Link`.
- **API Gateway Components -> Metrics & Telemetry Emitter**: Collects telemetry asynchronously via `AWS internal telemetry bus`.
- **API Gateway Access Logs -> Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Streams sanitized logs via `AWS Kinesis Data Firehose`.
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine -> AWS API Gateway**: Returns decisions via `gRPC`.
- **AWS API Gateway -> Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems**: Returns final responses via `HTTPS`.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS API Gateway HTTP API**: Chosen for low latency and cost-efficiency to meet the 50ms P99 budget.
- **AWS WAF**: Native edge security to satisfy PCI-DSS perimeter defense without custom code.
- **gRPC over HTTP/2**: High-performance binary protocol used for internal service communication to minimize serialization overhead.
- **AWS Kinesis Data Firehose & Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Provides tamper-evident, 7-year audit retention for regulatory compliance.
- **AWS Cloud Map**: Lightweight service discovery mechanism suited for a 3-engineer team.

## Rationale
This architecture uses fully managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while staying within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, tamper-evident 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms P99 latency via edge filtering and gRPC communication.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under 50 ms latency and manages analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
- API Router & Token Handler: Go component terminating gRPC and sanitizing card data.
- Feature Aggregator: Go component fetching data using Redis pipelining (`errgroup`).
- Decision Orchestrator: Go component coordinating ML inference and zero-downtime rules.
- Audit Logger & Cryptographic Signer: Go component signing decisions via AWS KMS.
- Metrics & Tracing Interceptor: Go middleware using `zerolog` for zero-allocation telemetry.
- ML Inference Service: Python with ONNX Runtime on AWS ECS Fargate.
- Amazon ElastiCache: Redis caching layer for fast feature lookups.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Operational database for transaction and authorization data.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident storage for 7-year audit compliance.

## Relationships
- AWS API Gateway -> API Router & Token Handler: Routes authorization requests [gRPC]
- API Router & Token Handler -> Feature Aggregator: Invokes feature lookup [In-memory Go calls]
- Feature Aggregator -> Amazon ElastiCache: Fetches user and card features [TCP (RESP)]
- Decision Orchestrator -> ML Inference Service: Requests model scoring [Internal gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Audit Logger & Cryptographic Signer -> Amazon DynamoDB: Persists audit records [HTTPS (AWS SDK v2)]
- Audit Logger & Cryptographic Signer -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Archives signed payloads [HTTPS (AWS SDK v2)]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency microservices and minimal GC overhead.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration matching the 3-engineer operational capacity.
- ONNX Runtime: High-performance machine learning model execution.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Scalable operational storage with persistent HTTPS connection pooling.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Write-once-read-many (WORM) storage for regulatory 7-year audit trails.
- AWS KMS: Hardware-backed cryptographic signing for tamper-evident audit logging.

## Rationale
This component architecture uses in-memory Go primitives and connection pooling to consistently achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. AWS serverless and container services keep operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team while satisfying strict PCI-DSS and auditability mandates.

- Amazon DynamoDB: Stores case data and audit trails with high availability and low latency.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year compliance audit logging.

## Rationale
The architecture strictly enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and sub-50ms P99 latency via asynchronous telemetry and optimized ONNX runtime execution. It operates reliably within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget managed by a three-engineer team.

## Overview
The Fraud Analyst Frontend is a React Single Page Application hosted on Amazon S3 and delivered via Amazon CloudFront, enabling fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions and update rules. It securely interfaces with backend services while enforcing strict PCI-DSS compliance and data redaction.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts: End users accessing the system interface.
- Authentication & Authorization Module: AWS Cognito integration enforcing OAuth2/OIDC role-based access control.
- Case Management Dashboard: React/TypeScript component rendering transaction queues and risk metadata.
- Audit Logging & Redaction Guard: Client-side proxy interceptor preventing raw card primary account numbers (PANs) from rendering in the DOM.
- Rule & Model Management Console: Administrative interface for zero-downtime rule and scoring model updates.
- WebSocket Client Module: Native browser client maintaining real-time queue synchronization.

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Fraud Analyst Frontend: Accesses review interface via HTTPS
- Authentication & Authorization Module -> AWS Cognito: OAuth2/OIDC authentication via HTTPS
- Case Management Dashboard -> Case Management Backend: Fetches review queues and submits decisions via REST/JSON over HTTPS
- Rule & Model Management Console -> Case Management Backend: Triggers rule adjustments and model deployments via REST/JSON over HTTPS
- WebSocket Client Module -> Case Management Backend: Receives real-time queue synchronization updates via WSS over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- React & TypeScript: Core frontend framework and type-safe language for robust UI development
- Tailwind CSS: Utility-first styling for rapid dashboard layout implementation
- TanStack Query (React Query): State management and API data caching to optimize network traffic
- AWS SDK for Browser: Integration toolkit for AWS service communication
- Native WebSocket API: Persistent connection layer for real-time updates

## Rationale
This component architecture fits the requirements by strictly isolating sensitive cardholder data on the client side to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance (R-05). Furthermore, centralizing all backend interactions through the Case Management Backend minimizes infrastructure complexity for a three-engineer team within a fixed budget.

Amazon EventBridge.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations and case management for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency while maintaining strict PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts, ML Engineers
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems, Card Networks / Token Vaults, Audit / Compliance Archive, ML Model / Rule Registry
- AWS API Gateway
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go on AWS ECS Fargate)
- ML Inference Service (Python with ONNX Runtime on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Go/Node.js on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Fraud Analyst Frontend (Amazon CloudFront and S3)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon S3 Object Lock
- Amazon EventBridge (Default Event Bus, Fraud Event Rules, Case Management Target, Audit Archive Target, Dead-Letter Queue)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> ML Inference Service: Requests feature scoring [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon ElastiCache: Fetches user velocity and card profiles [Redis Protocol / TCP]
- Default Event Bus -> Case Management Target: Dispatches filtered review events [AWS internal SQS]
- Default Event Bus -> Audit Archive Target: Streams decision logs [Kinesis Data Firehose / HTTPS]
- Audit Archive Target -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Stores immutable audit records [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Cloud (eu-west-1): Provides a fixed-budget, scalable infrastructure adhering to regional constraints.
- Go and Python (ONNX Runtime): Delivers high-performance scoring and low-latency machine learning inference.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Eliminates server management overhead for a three-engineer team.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit retention for regulatory compliance.
- Amazon EventBridge and SQS: Handles asynchronous, decoupled event routing reliably without blocking core scoring.

## Rationale
This serverless-first, asynchronous architecture protects the 50ms P99 scoring latency by offloading non-critical tasks. It satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 and stringent audit requirements while remaining operable within budget by a three-engineer team.
